key_insight: HEPTv2 is an end-to-end point-transformer that reconstructs charged-particle tracks directly from detector hits without graph building, clustering, or filtering.
engineering_relevance: It targets real-time, high-throughput tracking at the HL-LHC by improving the accuracy-latency trade-off while keeping memory and inference cost low on GPU hardware.
method: Locality-aware point encoder with locality-sensitive hashing in detector coordinate space
Sectorized track decoder with direct hit-to-track prediction
Joint encoder-decoder supervision for end-to-end optimization
evidence_signal: On TrackML, the model reports 98.6% double-majority tracking efficiency at a 0.8% fake rate, with about 15 ms inference time and 0.4 GB peak memory per event on an NVIDIA A100.
watch_item: Performance may depend on carefully tuned sectorization and locality hashing, which could affect robustness when detector conditions or hit densities change.
paper_title: HEPTv2: End-to-End Efficient Point Transformer for Charged Particle Reconstruction
